messages:
incident-bot: [P1] ALERT — latency SLO breach detected for /v1/streams (p99 > 2s). Auto-page on-call.

Robin: paging @Maya, @Sam — I'm going to take initial triage. Anyone already looking? :rotating_light:

Maya: on it. grabbing p95/p99 now. seeing streaming stalls in multiple regions.

Sam: checking infra metrics, hosts look healthy, no CPU/GPU throttling. network ok.

Maya: quick snapshot: p50=120ms, p95=480ms, p99=3.9s for /v1/streams in us-west-2. Streaming chunk stalls and long tail tokens reported.

Jonah: I see an abnormal drop in prefix cache hit rate starting ~2026-02-28T02:40Z. Hit rate -> 3% from ~85%. Could explain tail latency when KV cache misses and we recompute prefixes.

Maya: can you paste the cache metrics?

Jonah: sure:

```
prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.031
prefix_cache.requests: 12456
prefix_cache.misses: 12050
streaming.chunk_latency.p99: 3880ms
```

Sam: where is prefix cache backed? redis-cluster-2?

Jonah: yes, redis cluster. but redis ops look normal — keys not being evicted en masse.

Maya: dump a sample of keys for prefix:* pattern?

Sam: running: `redis-cli -c -h redis-primary --scan --pattern "prefix:*" | head -n 20`

Sam: result: empty. only new keys with `prefix_v2:` namespace are present. older `prefix:` keys missing.

Jonah: aha. we rolled a change yesterday that tweaked prefix hashing (commit abc123) to use a newer canonicalization (v2) but didn't migrate the cache. rollout was canary->global. looks like new runtime writes new key namespace and misses the old cache entries.

Maya: that explains sudden low hit rate. requests for older keys are missing so runtime recomputes heavy prefixes causing stalls.

Robin: customer impact? Elaine, any CS reports?

Elaine: got one ticket from Customer X about streaming stalls around 02:45Z. They reported repeated stalled tokens and reconnects for a 10-12s window. No billing impact reported yet.

Maya: mitigation options:
- roll back the prefix-hash change globally (fast but touches many pods)
- patch runtime to compute legacy hash in-flight (hotfix) and write both key formats (safer)
- force-cache-fill script to populate new keys from existing cache entries (risky)

Sam: I can do a quick rollback of the model-proc config for canary and then global if needed. rollback command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-proc -n prod --to-revision=123`

Jonah: hotfix to write both key formats is low-risk but takes 20–30m to build+deploy.

Robin: prioritize fastest safe mitigation. roll back the prefix-hash change for now, then follow with a patch. Sam, execute rollback but do canary first?

Sam: rolling back canary now. watching deployment.

incident-bot: Incident update — rollback started by Sam.

Maya: keeping an eye on p99:

```
Before rollback: p99=3900ms
Canary rollback (3 pods): p99 -> 1200ms
Global rollback in progress...
```

Sam: global rollback complete. model-proc pods back to v1-hash on all nodes.

Maya: cache hit rate recovering — current prefix_cache.hit_rate: 72% and climbing. streaming stalls subsiding. p99 now ~310ms.

Elaine: reported customer issue resolved for Customer X. they confirmed streaming responsiveness returned. 

Robin: good. now the post-incident plan:
- root cause: prefix hash/namespace change (commit abc123) deployed without cache migration and no compatibility layer.
- immediate mitigation: rollback deployed at 02:56Z.
- follow-up: implement dual-write hotfix (runtime writes both legacy and v2 keys), add a migration job to populate v2 keys, add e2e test to cover cache key namespace compatibility.

Jonah: opening a PR for the dual-write hotfix and will request expedited review. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/model-proc/pull/456 (WIP).

Maya: creating postmortem issue: https://issues.redwood/INC-2026-02-prefix-cache. Assigning action items.

Robin: handoff — @Maya you'll be on-call for the next shift to follow up on migration job and monitor hit rate. @Sam please keep an eye on rollback metrics and any regression during rollback window.

Maya: ack. I'll also prepare a short runbook snippet for future prefix-key changes.

Sam: noted. I'll run a verification job to ensure no split-brain keys remain: `python tools/verify_prefix_keys.py --env prod`

Jonah: log note: root cause requires adding a gating check to our rollout pipeline: if cache namespace changes, require explicit migration flag.

Robin: closing incident thread once postmortem and PR are in place. Good work everyone. :heart:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — latency SLO returned within thresholds. Incident duration ~16 minutes.

Maya: filing timeline and attaching charts. will ping when PR is merged and migration job scheduled.

Elaine: reaching out proactively to the affected customer with a summary.

Jonah: action items summary (short):
- PR dual-write hotfix (#456) — Jonah — P0 -> merge + canary
- migration job to populate v2 keys — Maya/Sam — run and verify
- rollout pipeline guard for namespace changes — Engineering Practices — backlog item
- postmortem doc and customer communication — Maya/ELAINE

Robin: thanks all. signing off from active triage.
